shear-flow.look: Warped FBm reads as smoke and marble: long curving fibres and sharp veins with even detail everywhere, and no plateaus or crease knots. Relief shows continuous combed slopes and layered mesas, not the round lake plateaus and terraces of warped gradient; as terrain it reads wind sheared, not natural. At 1 step it shows straight bands and at 2 a crosshatch; on an FBm source both are gone by 3. Direction=Periodic3 at 9 to 21 steps gives curling smoke with spiral eyes, which is the most distinctive mode. Golden directions, as first proposed, give a visible global streak per seed; the perpendicular pairs table I tried removes it. On a regular source (stripes) at 64 unit window at lac 1, long cross cutting fault lines from the 1D noise show; lac 1.3 or more reduced them. 3D volumes are lamellar sheets, flatter than Feistel with 1D noise and less flat with the noise2 option.
shear-flow.dims: 2D rendered and measured. 3D rendered with slice and vol, det 0.995 to 1.003. 4D measured det 0.991 to 1.011 over 4000 points, and a 2x2 torus tile image is seamless.
shear-flow.range: Source range unchanged: -0.994..1.007 over 8 seeds with my FBm scale. Warp only, no node range of its own.
shear-flow.artifacts: Straight fault lines on regular sources at lac 1. Thin aliasing filaments at high amplitude.
shear-flow.node_shape: One node, working name DomainWarpShear, in the DomainWarp family: Source, Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Feature Scale, Steps (int), Lacunarity, Gain, Kernel enum {Noise, Parabola, Sine}, Direction enum {Pairs, Golden, Periodic3}, Seed Offset. No Birkhoff output.
shear-flow.port_notes: Constant count loop, branch free: dot, 2 hashes, quintic per step. Latency bound: measured 1.0 to 1.15 ns per step against the idea's 0.3 to 0.5. Nearly flat across dimensions. Seed rotation needs a seed hash plus sin and cos per batch and is not in the kernel numbers; without it 24 seeds share a grain direction (concentration 0.98 versus 0.12). Hybrid amplitude breaks det=1: det sd 0.34 at +-50 percent, 8.7 at +-100 percent, measured on the parabola chain. The scalar ratio includes the 5 octave source, about 254 of the 370 ns. Birkhoff measured 37x Perlin scalar (30 steps, 3 octave source) for islands in a grainy sea at amp 0.8 and mostly grain at 1.2: not worth it.

critic.notes: Re-ran check and speed: c0ratio 7.26, 359 ns scalar = 7.28x perlin2 (includes the 5 octave source). Real node bench matches the prototyper: DomainWarpGradient 0.93/1.76/3.47, prog3 3.06/5.14/10.22, Perlin 0.90/2.12/4.10 ns AVX2. Seed 21 window 8 and seed 7 window 32 both give combed smoke and marble, wide views uniform with no repeat. Without seed rotation seeds 1 to 3 share one grain direction, confirmed. Steps sweep at seed 21: 2 steps shows a fine crosshatch, 3 and up clean. Stripes at seed 21 window 48: wavy stripes, no wallpaper; the regular feel is mostly the stripes themselves. det=1 vs Gradient holds visually: in the rms 1 family sheets the Gradient replica shows plateaus, rectangles and terraces, the chains show even fibres, and the equal area checker keeps cell areas. The 3D volume is torn lamellar sheets (1D kernel), a real 3D weakness; the noise2 option is needed there. Not cheap: about 6 ns warp only in 2D (prototyper estimate, not verified by me) against 3.06 ns measured for progressive Gradient 3; the case for it is no folds at high amplitude and near flat cost across dimensions. A 6 octave progressive Simplex graph gives crinkled foil and blown blobs with fold rings, not combed fibres, so the look is not reachable from existing nodes. Kernel enum should be Noise and Parabola only, Direction Pairs and Periodic3 only.
critic.improved: Tried the hybrid mix (2 or 3 noise steps then parabola shears) to cut cost: on a stripe source at window 48 the parabola tail still reads as a regular zigzag textile, on FBm it is identical to the pure noise chain. Not adopted. Periodic3 should default to 9 steps: at seed 7, 21 steps gives c0ratio 1.5 and max slope 733 (aliasing filaments), 9 steps gives c0ratio 6.0 with clean curls. Gallery files not changed.

tournament.notes: Re-ran check and speed: c0ratio 7.26, 359 ns scalar = 7.28x perlin2 including the 5 octave source. Seed 21 window 8 and seed 7 window 32 both give combed smoke and marble with uniform wide views. Seeds share one grain direction without table rotation, confirmed. 2 steps show a fine crosshatch, 3 and up clean. Stripes at seed 21 window 48: wavy stripes, no wallpaper. det=1 vs Gradient holds visually in the rms 1 sheets (plateaus and terraces vs even fibres, equal area checker cells). 3D volume is torn lamellar sheets from the 1D kernel; noise2 needed there. Not cheap: about 6 ns warp only in 2D by the prototyper's unverified estimate against 3.06 ns measured for progressive Gradient 3; the case is no folds at high amplitude and flat cost across dimensions. A 6 octave progressive Simplex graph gives crinkled foil with fold rings, so the look is not a graph recipe. Kernel Noise and Parabola only, Direction Pairs and Periodic3 only.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE from hand written AVX2 kernels, warp only, fixed seed, not FastSIMD: 6 steps 6.06/6.51/7.07, 8 steps 8.64/9.22/9.98, 12 steps 13.77/14.70/15.74 (2D/3D/4D). Add Source.

artist-terrain.note: Combed smoke and marble with even detail, no plateaus (det=1). Relief reads wind-sheared, not natural. ~6 ns 2D estimate; quality case, not price.

artist-material.note: Combed smoke and marble with long sweeping grain that stock warps do not reach. Immediately useful.

voxel-engineer.note: Even combed smoke with det 1. Vol is torn lamellae without the noise2 option. 6/6.5/7 ns est plus source, so flat in dimension.

maintainer.note: Combed smoke and marble, uniform wide view; but 6 ns warp-only est is twice DomainWarpFractalProgressive and the look overlaps existing warps. One DomainWarp node with a pairs table, nothing bigger.

graphics-researcher.note: Clean combed marble with no per-seed grain once the perpendicular-pairs table is used; equal-area and exactly invertible. Not cheap, not new as a map, but the cleanest smoke/marble warp here.

creative.note: Smoky silk with even fibres, better than the warps in the existing sheet.

plan_node.why_difficulty: Constant-count loop, branch free. Seed rotation is per lane, so the position turns into the table's frame and back rather than the table turning.

Noise 3 steps 3.17 / 5.91 / 6.25, 6 steps 5.54 / 10.40 / 10.81, 8 steps 7.13 / 13.31 / 13.64, 12 steps 10.10 / 19.01 / 19.32. Parabola 6 steps 3.39 / 4.28 / 4.94, 8 steps 4.27 / 5.21 / 5.97. Periodic 3 at 9 steps 7.89 / 8.56 / 8.93. Add Source. DomainWarpGradient 0.94 / 1.77 / 3.43, Progressive 3 over it 3.12 / 5.26 / 10.43.
plan_node.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D are real forms. 2D 1D noise per shear, 3D and 4D 2D noise per shear, since 1D noise showed flat sheets in 3D and rosettes through the torus map in 4D. Det J on the real node 0.998 to 1.002 in 2D, 0.991 to 1.010 in 3D, p0.1 to p99.9, 0 folded. 4D det not measured on the real node, the prototype read 0.991 to 1.011. Tile seamless.
plan_node.range: Warp: output is the Source's, no ScaleOutput. Warp Amplitude is the distance of the first step, measured typical move 0.44 x in 2D and 0.48 x in 3D at the defaults, longest 1.32 x, Parabola about 2 x that.
notes: Prototype amp maps as Warp Amplitude = amp x Feature Scale. The prototype unit is 64 world units at fnlab sizes, so per=2,amp=0.6,freq=0.3 is Feature Scale 213, Warp Amplitude 128, Source Feature Scale 64. Default 50 over 100 is strain 0.5.
Measured limits: strain 1.5 per step 0 to 1 of 4000 above 0.02, strain 2 88 of 4000 and a slope when followed, no feature set FAIL. Far coordinates clean to 1e7 world units.
The case is quality, not price: at equal rms displacement Gradient folds into plateaus while this keeps even fibres and equal cell areas.
Seed rotation is required, otherwise 24 seeds share a grain direction (concentration 0.98 vs 0.12). Hybrid amplitude breaks det=1.

absorbs.how: Kernel Parabola for FBm-like sources only; Sine should not exist per the critic
2D noise per shear as the 3D default; nothing else of its own

master.one_liner: A chain of 1D-noise shears: an exactly area-preserving warp at about 1/3 Perlin per step that behaves like fluid mixing (marbling), and in periodic mode gives KAM islands inside a chaotic sea.
master.look: Verified in prototype. Final sampling: pulled ink filaments, fine marbling folds without any pinched blobs. Periodic A=0.5: smooth contour-following streams. A=0.8: marble with lens-shaped smooth islands wrapped in fine layered filaments. A=1.2: smooth islands in a grainy sea with zig-zag strata. Good for marble, agate, ink, gas giants, mixed fluids, wood.
master.algorithm: Table of unit directions u_k with perpendicular t_k (Golden mode: angle k*2.39996; Periodic mode: k mod 3 x 60 degrees). For k in 0..N-1: s=dot(p,t_k); p+=u_k*A*gradnoise1(s*F, seed+salt_k). Since the displacement along u depends only on the perpendicular coordinate, every step has det J = 1. Output options: Warp() displacement; Source(p); Birkhoff average sum w_k*Source(p_k)/sum w_k with w(t)=exp(-1/(t(1-t))), whose super-convergence separates islands (smooth) from chaotic sea (grainy). In 3D/4D, s can be a 2D perpendicular noise for richer sheets. Prototypes: dyn_lens mode=6,N=10; mode=7,N=30,A=0.8.
master.why_new: Existing warps compress and pinch, and fold features with visible stretching blur; this preserves area exactly, so sampled densities stay statistically unchanged (no range or contrast collapse) and scalar sources keep their distribution. Very cheap per step, which allows N=12..30 where nested Simplex warps cannot afford it. Islands plus chaos in one field is a phase-space structure that single-pass noise never gives.
master.simd_plan: 1D gradient noise plus dot and add: about 0.3..0.5 ns per step. N=12: about 5 ns plus source. Birkhoff with a source sample every period (N/3 samples): 8..12 Perlin total. Direction table per node (computed once). Dimension-agnostic: use a D-dim direction list, ideally a low-discrepancy set. 4D cost barely grows, excellent for tiling. Warp() fits the existing interface.
master.continuity: C1 or C2 for the map (quintic 1D noise); composition keeps smoothness, with Lipschitz growing exponentially at high A. Birkhoff output is continuous but grainy in the chaotic regime.
master.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Shear Frequency, Steps, Direction Mode enum (Golden, Periodic 3), Output enum (Warp, Sample, Birkhoff), Source.
master.risks: 1D noise has lines of constant s, so low N shows straight-ish shear artefacts; N>=8 hides them. Periodic mode with 3 dirs shows faint zig-zag axis structure in the chaotic sea. Birkhoff is costly at N=30.
master.cost_note: 1D gradient noise plus dot and add: about 0.3..0.5 ns per step. N=12: about 5 ns plus source.

queue.name: ShearFlow
queue.reason: 1D-noise shear chain with det exactly 1, ~6 ns at N=12, flat across dimensions (J4 top pick). Also the base lyapunov-stretch needs, which earns it a slot beside domain-warp-sine.

lyapunov-stretch.look: Combed hair and feather barbs: bright flowing fibre bundles split by dark branching creases, unlike the thin ribbon marble of the same warp with a ridged source (side by side in shears_stretch_vs_ridged). Relief is striking: overlapping curved plates like eroded strata. Threshold at the median is flame or feather shapes. My first settings had straight diagonal bands across the wide view and a bright line in the FFT; making strain rise with frequency removed the bands. Not the thin veins on a dark background the idea promised at these settings: it reads brighter and more fibrous, and dark creases are the sharp feature. With the parabola kernel, 12 steps, it turns into dense fur.
lyapunov-stretch.dims: 2D rendered with Frobenius and single tangent forms (same layout, some bands differ). 3D uses a single tangent vector; the slice matches the 2D look and vol shows plates. 4D tangent form rendered through the torus map, tile seamless.
lyapunov-stretch.range: 1 - 2(1 + v.v)^-k gives analytic [-1,1) with no measured constant. Measured -0.999..0.722, mean -0.28 over 8 seeds.
lyapunov-stretch.artifacts: FFT keeps a weak star, grain R about 0.06. Thin lines alias at amp near 1 with many steps (amp 1, 16 steps gives c0ratio 1.5). Parabola with the pairs table goes woven, which is plaid.
lyapunov-stretch.node_shape: Separate generator sharing the shear-flow kernel, since it takes no Source: Steps, Amplitude, Feature Scale, Lacunarity, Gain, Kernel, Direction, Contrast k, Output Min/Max, Seed Offset.
lyapunov-stretch.port_notes: No source evaluations. The tangent update is off the critical latency path, so it is nearly free: including the log, noise 8 is +1.27 ns and noise 12 is +1.32 ns over warp only. Total is about 1.25 ns per step with noise against the idea's 0.7. Use 1 + v.v: the plain tangent form grows dark seams where the vector contracts. k=0.25 replaces the log with two square roots, not benchmarked separately.

critic.notes: Re-ran check and speed: c0ratio 6.44, max slope 83, 143 ns scalar = 2.88x perlin2. The headline look holds at the working window: combed hair and feather barbs, striking plate relief. The prototyper's claim that rising strain removes the bands is only half true: at seed 21 window 12 the wide view is a woven basket (axis 25) and at seed 1337 a diagonal hatch; the stretch of a 1D shear is constant along lines, so the two strongest directions always show. This is plaid, the family's named failure, but at the feature scale it reads as the fibre direction a fur or brushed material wants. 3D works but is softer and blurrier than 2D (single tangent), the volume is layered plates. A graph of existing nodes gets only single direction hair (DomainAxisScale of ridged Perlin under a progressive Simplex warp: wavy vertical strands at amp 20, swirled bundles with ring folds at amp 40), not locally combed fibres with branching creases. Ship as a separate generator sharing the shear kernel; document the hatch.
critic.improved: Tried to remove the wide view weave: warm=2 and 3 (first steps warp but do not feed the tangent), golden table instead of pairs, gain 1.0 and 1.05, lac 1.15, 12 steps, each at seed 21 window 40. Straight lines soften but a herringbone hatch stays in every variant (axis 16 to 42). The softest variant (golden, warm 2, gain 1.05) also squashes the range to max 0.14 and loses the barbs. Gallery files not changed.

tournament.notes: Re-ran check and speed: c0ratio 6.44, max slope 83, 143 ns scalar = 2.88x perlin2. The look holds at the working window: combed hair and feather barbs, striking plate relief. The rising strain claim is half true: at seed 21 window 12 the wide view is a woven basket (axis 25), at seed 1337 a diagonal hatch; the stretch of a 1D shear is constant along lines so the two strongest directions always show. This is plaid, but at feature scale it is the fibre direction a fur or brushed material wants. 3D is softer and blurrier than 2D (single tangent), volume is layered plates. The existing node fur recipe gives only single direction hair with ring folds. Ship as a separate generator sharing the shear kernel, document the hatch.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE from hand written AVX2 kernels with tangent vector and log(1 + v.v), not FastSIMD: noise 8 steps 9.91/10.65/11.44, noise 12 15.09/16.23/17.41, parabola 8 4.68/5.53/6.73, parabola 12 7.66/8.86/10.41.

artist-material.note: Feather barbs and hair strands with strong dark lines, and it needs no source. The plate relief is odd, the 2D map is excellent.

voxel-engineer.note: Beautiful hair in 2D thumb; plaid at wide view, blurry in 3D. A material, not world gen.

maintainer.note: Striking relief of overlapping curved plates like eroded strata, 2.9x Perlin scalar; c0 6.4 with slope 83 and one shared grain direction per seed. An output of the shear chain rather than a node.

graphics-researcher.note: Stretch field of a shear chain as a texture is new maths for noise: combed hair with branching dark creases, and a relief of overlapping curved plates that is one of the best images in the set, at 2.9x Perlin. Woven wide view with the pairs table is the honest flaw.

creative.note: Calligraphic brush streaks and paddy-terrace relief. The fur and agate discoveries show its range.

Parabola 8 steps 5.03 / 5.76 / 7.15, 12 steps 7.10 / 7.83 / 9.71. Periodic 3 at 9 steps 9.04 / 8.63 / 10.28. Contrast 0.4 instead of 0.25 8.51 / 14.90 / 16.26.

absorbs.how: the node; own class since it takes no Source

master.one_liner: Propagates the analytic Jacobian through a shear chain and outputs log stretch (finite-time Lyapunov exponent), drawing the invisible veins of a mixing flow as thin filament networks at very low cost.
master.look: Verified in prototype. Dark background with bright thin curling filaments and fibre bundles, like Lagrangian coherent structures in ocean currents, fine marble veins or hair flow. N=10 Golden is broader and streakier; periodic N=21..30 gives cleaner thread-like veins. Hillshade reads as combed fur or wind streaks. Good for veins, cirrus, flow fields, fur masks, wood grain detail.
master.algorithm: J=I. For each shear k of ShearFlow: compute d=A*n(s), ds=A*F*n'(s) analytically; p+=u*d; J=(I + ds*u*t^T)*J. Output Scale*log(||J||_F^2) - Offset. Cheaper option: propagate one tangent vector v=(I+ds*u*t^T)v only and output log(v.v), with no Frobenius matrix; after a few steps it aligns with the max stretch direction. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=25,N=12,A=0.6,per=1,k=0.3,o=0.5.
master.why_new: Ridged and warped noises make lines at contour levels of a warped field; here lines are places of maximum strain in the map and are thin because of exponential growth, not due to thresholding. Gradient-flow FTLE was tried and is grainy; the shear chain's exact analytic Jacobian is what makes it clean and cheap.
master.simd_plan: Each step: 1D noise with derivative plus 2x2 matrix update (or 2 mul-adds for tangent form): about 0.7 ns. N=12: about 8 ns, N=21: about 15 ns. 3D/4D: single tangent vector form keeps it near-linear in D. No source evals at all, a pure generator.
master.continuity: C0 and smooth since log(||J||^2) is smooth with ||J||>=1 for area-preserving maps. Measured c0ratio 3.3 and max slope about 460 per unit at N=12.
master.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Shear Frequency, Steps, Direction Mode, Output Scale. Mixins: Feature Scale, VariableRange.
master.risks: Output is positive-skewed; normalisation by a measured constant varies with N and A. Periodic mode is not fully isotropic. Very thin veins alias at low sample rate.
master.cost_note: Each step: 1D noise with derivative plus 2x2 matrix update (or 2 mul-adds for tangent form): about 0.7 ns.

queue.name: LyapunovStretch
queue.reason: Analytic Jacobian through a shear chain gives filament veins at ~0.7 ns per step (J4 top pick). Exists only as a shear-flow output; replaces stretch-ftle at a fraction of the cost.

stretch-ftle.look: Three different results. On a shear chain, finite difference FTLE is visually the same image as the analytic lyapunov-stretch, at 2.8x the scalar cost (542 vs 191 ns at 12 steps), so analytic wins there. Curl flow: thin bright curling worms and spirals wrapped round vortices, a brain coral look nothing else in this family makes, and it only works at low eta with one octave: at eta 0.25 and 2 octaves it is pure grain. Gradient flow: a closed cell network with thin bright boundaries and dark flat basins, topologically close to warped CellularDistance F1-F2 but with rounder cells and steeper lines. It is not the dendritic tree the catalogue entry first promised, which matches the FlowSeparatrix note.
stretch-ftle.dims: 2D rendered. 3D by finite differences: gradient flow vol is an open cell foam; curl flow 3D slice shows thin lines on dark, no vol rendered. 4D not attempted.
stretch-ftle.range: Not normalised. Curl -1.02..2.19, gradient -2.76..2.60 where -2.76 is the log clamp, so dark basins are flat plateaus. Needs a measured constant per setting.
stretch-ftle.artifacts: Curl 3D z-continuity max 0.73 for dz=1e-3, very steep. Gradient c0ratio 2.45 with max slope 600 per unit, lines one pixel wide.
stretch-ftle.node_shape: Not a member of this family's node. If kept, an Output enum of a flow node: Steps, Step Length, Field enum, Contrast, Output Min/Max. The shear chain case is served by lyapunov-stretch.
stretch-ftle.port_notes: Propagating the Jacobian with the analytic Perlin Hessian beats the idea's twin trajectories: 624 versus 1692 ns scalar at N=12, same image, no epsilon. At 4e4 coordinates finite differences degrade (std 0.80, min at the clamp) while the Hessian form stays at std 0.38. It works only on a built in noise, since nodes expose no Hessian.

critic.notes: Re-ran: curl flow 632 ns scalar = 12.3x perlin2, c0ratio 5.3, max slope 241, 3D z-continuity max 0.73 for dz=1e-3; gradient flow 470 ns = 9.3x, c0ratio 2.45, max slope 601, range -2.76..2.60 unnormalised. Curl flow at seed 21 window 10 confirms thin curling worms and spirals, brain coral, with a uniform wide view; nothing in the catalogue makes this. Gradient flow cells are close to warped CellularDistance F1-F2 which is a graph recipe already. FD FTLE of a shear chain is the same image as analytic lyapunov-stretch (family sheet), so that case is served. Fingerprint cells are fun but c0ratio 1.7 and 3D unsolved. Port needs an analytic Perlin Hessian per step on a built in noise (no node exposes one), est 25 to 36 ns in 2D and much more in 3D: too costly and niche for a regular node, worth an example.

tournament.notes: Re-ran: curl flow 632 ns scalar = 12.3x perlin2, c0ratio 5.3, max slope 241, 3D z-continuity max 0.73 for dz=1e-3; gradient flow 470 ns = 9.3x, c0ratio 2.45, max slope 601, range -2.76..2.60 unnormalised. Curl flow at seed 21 window 10 confirms thin curling worms and spirals (brain coral) with a uniform wide view; nothing in the catalogue makes this. Gradient flow cells are close to warped CellularDistance F1-F2, already a graph recipe. FD FTLE of a shear chain equals analytic lyapunov-stretch. Fingerprint cells are fun but c0ratio 1.7 and 3D unsolved. Port needs an analytic Perlin Hessian per step on a built in noise, est 25 to 36 ns 2D and far more in 3D: an example, not a node.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, no kernel written: analytic Hessian form about 2 to 3 ns per step, so 25 to 36 ns at N=12 and 16 to 24 ns at N=8 in 2D. 3D finite difference gradient flow measured 2943 ns scalar, 29x perlin3, so about 60 ns by that ratio. Curl in 3D needs two gradient fields, about double. 4D not estimated.

artist-terrain.note: Curl-flow brain coral and basin-foam vol are unique; 12x Perlin, c0 5.3, 3D z-jumps 0.73, port 3.

artist-material.note: Veined cell plates like turtle shell in 2D, and the 3D basin foam is beautiful. Costly and has steep spots.

voxel-engineer.note: Foam vol is pretty, c0 low, about 60 ns est in 3D. Graph gets close on the cells.

maintainer.note: Finite-difference FTLE is lyapunov-stretch at 2.8x; curl-flow brain coral is unique but 12x Perlin with max slope 241 and 3D z jumps.

graphics-researcher.note: Curl-flow FTLE gives brain-coral worms and spirals nothing else makes; the FTLE fingerprint cells and basin foam volume are two of the strangest images of the tournament. Expensive and steep, but port 3 undersells it.

creative.note: Flowing lines trapped in cells, and the fingerprint discovery is excellent. Has moire patches in the volume.

master.one_liner: Finite-time Lyapunov exponent of the N-step flow map: thin sharp filaments (Lagrangian coherent structures) for curl fields, dendritic watershed divides for gradient fields.
master.look:
Curl field: braided, sharply defined ribbons and filaments wrapping around vortex cores, like dye visualisations of 2D turbulence; the ridges are one line wide while interiors are smooth, which no fractal gives. Gradient field: a continuous dendritic network of divide lines (the ridgelines of fBm as thin crisp curves, branching tree-like), i.e. a true ridge/divide detector, far cleaner than FractalRidged, and usable as a mask for ridges, crack lines, lightning, root systems.
[FlowSeparatrix, terrain-landforms] Thin bright closed-cell network tracing the source's valley floors and separating each peak's basin, with occasional dangling arms. Carving it produces sharp incised lines. Good for crack-like valleys, river masks that agree with terrain, and watershed-cell partitioning.
master.algorithm:
Trace d+1 twin trajectories through the same flow as FlowWatershed/StirAdvect: q_0 = Phi(p0), q_i = Phi(p0 + eps*e_i), i=1..d, all with the same fixed N steps.
  J[:,i] = (q_i - q_0)/eps                       // Jacobian of the flow map by finite differences (no Hessian needed)
  2D: S = ||J||_F^2, D = det J, sigma_max^2 = (S + sqrt(S^2 - 4 D^2)) / 2
  3D/4D: use ||J||_F^2 / d as the stretch proxy, or two power-iteration steps of J^T J on a hashed start vector
  out = log(sigma_max) / (N*h), remapped by a measured constant; Direction enum: Forward (repelling structures) / Backward (attracting, negate field).
For gradient-descent fields the repelling set is the watershed divide; for curl fields it is the stretching skeleton of the stirring.
master.why_new: Measures sensitivity of the flow map, which needs the flow map evaluated at d+1 nearby points: inexpressible in a graph. It extracts topological structure (divides, stretching manifolds) that single-pass noise never has. Shares the FlowEngine; could be an Output enum of the flow node rather than a separate class.
master.simd_plan: (d+1) full trajectories each with the flow's per-step evals; closed-form 2x2 singular value or Frobenius norm; log via FS::Log; no masks. Cost ~ (d+1) x flow cost: 2D N=8 analytic-gradient engine ~3 x 13 = ~40x Perlin (~45 ns); 3D ~4 x 85 = ~340 ns; 4D ~5 x 220 = ~1.1 us. Heavy in 4D; recommend 2D/3D use, but it is dimension-agnostic and correct. When a user DomainWarp node is the field, call its Warp() d+1 times per step.
master.continuity: Continuous (log of a smooth positive quantity, finite-difference Jacobian of a smooth map), C1 with analytic gradients; very steep at the ridges by design.
master.params: Same as the flow node (Field/Potential, Steps, StepLen, FieldType enum Gradient/Curl/WarpSource) plus Epsilon float (1e-3..1e-2 feature), Direction enum, Measure enum (SigmaMax / Frobenius), Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Cost; ridge contrast depends on N*h (too short: blurry, too long: everything saturates); eps must stay > floating error of far coordinates (use 1e-2 feature at large world coords).
[FlowSeparatrix, terrain-landforms] TESTED in numpy. It produces closed cells, NOT dendritic trees, so it does not by itself solve river networks. Unit-length stepping produced contour-like ring artifacts; deceleration removed them. Fine lines need antialiasing or a larger dx, and the carve looks scratched when thin. Applying it to many-octave sources was not tested.

domain-warp-sine.look: Same family of look as the noise chain on FBm: wispy, feathery smoke fibres that get finer with octave count, with swirling fold bundles at amp 1 and up. Plaid at low octaves is real: oct 1 straight bands, oct 2 crosshatch, gone from oct 3 on an FBm source. The real flaw is on regular sources: warped stripes at oct 4 are practically the same image at a lag of (-97.25, 71.75), the wide view is wallpaper, and oct 8 and 16 still read as a regular textile. On FBm the literal repeat is hidden because the source is aperiodic, though the wide panel still has an even swirl rhythm. The parabolic wave looks nearly identical to true sine and costs one third, so true sine has no reason to exist.

master.one_liner: Iterated rotated sine shears: an exactly area-preserving, lattice-free fluid warp at a fraction of simplex warp cost.
master.look: Smooth folded ribbons, ink in water, flowing marble when applied to a stripe source. No lattice imprint. Look-tested (mode 15): strong fluid-like folds, clearly different from Warp Gradient and Warp Simplex on the sheet, which show pinched highlights.
master.algorithm: freq = 1/Scale. For i in 0..Octaves-1: phase = freq*dot(p, n_i) + phi_i(seed); p += Amp * d_i * sin(phase) / freq; freq *= Lacunarity (default 1.4). Then Source(p). n_i and d_i are orthonormal pairs from a constant table: 2D rotates by (0.6, 0.8) each octave; 3D and 4D use precomputed irrational axes. phi_i from seed hash bits plus i. Each step is a shear, so Jacobian det = 1 + g'*(d.n) = 1 exactly: pointwise area-preserving in any dimension, no pinch, and the Source histogram is preserved.
master.why_new: Existing warps cost a noise evaluation per axis or per octave and have lattice signature plus pinch-related contrast change. This one is orders of magnitude simpler per octave, has no hash per lattice corner and leaves range and histogram unchanged, which makes it safe to insert into any graph. Not reachable by a graph because each iteration depends on the previous position.
master.simd_plan: Constant-octave loop with one FS::Sin + one dot per octave and no branches. Estimated about 3 ns AVX2 for 8 octaves + Source in any dimension (scalar prototype inflated by std::sin at 5.5x Perlin including 1 Perlin). Dim-agnostic via table of pairs. Seed via a single hash per call then bit-shifted per octave. 4D is automatically tile-safe.
master.continuity: The map is C-infinity, so output has the continuity of Source. Measured c0ratio 8.0.
master.params: Source, Octaves (int), Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Feature Scale, Lacunarity, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Quasi-periodic at low octave counts (visible plaid). Direction table is constant so seeds change only phases, and different seeds can look related at large scale. High amplitude gives thin filaments that alias. A hybrid amplitude loses exact area preservation (d*g becomes spatially modulated). SIMD Sin accuracy at far coordinates needs checking; scalar check at 4e4 was fine.
[DomainWarpSine, shader-community] Large amplitudes fold the domain (overlaps), as with any warp; visible 1D-wave structure at Layers<3. Sine phase precision far from origin (use range-reduced Sin, same as SineWave).
master.cost_note: Estimated about 3 ns AVX2 for 8 octaves + Source in any dimension (scalar prototype inflated by std::sin at 5.5x Perlin including 1 Perlin).
master.variant_notes: The Xor-style form displaces each axis by a sine of another rotated axis; the shear form here is what gives exact area preservation.

master.one_liner: Domain warp built from coordinate shears: exactly area/volume preserving and invertible at any amplitude, so warping never folds, never changes coverage and never changes topology.
master.look: Warped checkerboard: organic jigsaw cells of exactly equal area. Warped fBm at high Amp: long marbled lamellae with no pinched or inflated zones. Good for marble, fluid mixing, equal-area biome cells, and warping any mask without changing its coverage. Measured unit-cell area after warp: Feistel Amp 0.8 mean 1.000 std 0.001 max 1.005; Amp 1.6 mean 1.000 std 0.001 max 1.004. Additive vector warp: Amp 0.8 mean 1.149 std 0.452 max 3.58; Amp 1.6 mean 1.206 std 0.773 max 6.10 (upper two thirds of cells by area).
master.algorithm: For r in Rounds: for each axis i: pos[i] += Amp * S_r,i(pos with coordinate i replaced by a per-round constant). Then apply a fixed rotation (golden angle in 2D, fixed orthonormal matrix in 3D/4D). Each shear has Jacobian determinant exactly 1 and an exact inverse (subtract in reverse order), for any source S and any Amp, which is the Feistel network construction. Rotations also have determinant 1. Evaluate the warped source at the final position.
master.why_new: Existing warps add a vector, which folds when the gradient of the warp exceeds 1, and they change local area, so a warped threshold no longer has the source's coverage. Curl-noise warps approximate incompressibility and need integration and gradients. Shears are exact with no gradient, and exact in 2D, 3D and 4D alike. A warped CellularValue or Checkerboard gives equal-area organic cells, which is otherwise a hard global problem.
master.simd_plan: Rounds*D source evals: R=3 gives 6 / 9 / 12. One source call per axis with coordinate i set to a constant, no lane-dependent flow. Using Simplex or Perlin as the shear source is about 6-12x Perlin; measured 12x perlin2 scalar including a 3-octave fBm source evaluation. Rotations are constant-matrix FMulAdd. Fits the DomainWarp Warp() interface or a modifier over a source. 4D tiling is preserved because shears are periodic functions of periodic inputs.
master.continuity: As smooth as the shear source: C1 or better with Perlin, and C1 in the composite. The downstream source's own discontinuities are preserved.
master.params: Amp (hybrid), Rounds (int), Shear Source (GeneratorSource, or built-in Simplex with Frequency), Source. Hybrid Amp breaks exactness only if Amp depends on the sheared coordinate, so document that it should be a constant or low-frequency.
master.risks: Axis-aligned shears show through at few rounds, which the rotation mitigates. At high Amp, thin lamellae alias on coarse grids. Exactness holds for measure, not for local shape, which can stretch hard. If the source ignores a fixed coordinate there is no problem, but a hybrid Amp varying along the sheared axis breaks exactness. Only 2D was run.
master.cost_note: Using Simplex or Perlin as the shear source is about 6-12x Perlin; measured 12x perlin2 scalar including a 3-octave fBm source evaluation.
